doc_base: 65 (Phase I cap set by Preliminary Plan 120020220; zone figure is 156 du with MPDUs = 4.39 du/ac x 35.74 ac Phase I gross, i.e. ~128 before bonus)
doc_base_quote: Approval under this preliminary plan is limited to the following: a. Phase I - fifty-three (53) one family detached and twelve (12) one family attached residential units, including nine (9) MPDU’s.
reason_quote: Staff has worked with the Town and applicant to provide a predominantly one family detached mix of units for this phase that staff believes to be compatible with the Town.
comment: Site plan data table is image-only (82006012__102507_piedmont.pdf p. 16, read from PDF): Max. Density 4.39 du/ac = 156 d.u.s Permitted, 1.73 du/ac = 62 proposed, on 35.74 ac Phase I gross (net site 11.80 ac after 2.66 ac streets and 21.28 ac park/legacy open space); Number of Dwelling Units Total permitted = "65 per Preliminary Plan". So our 127.8 (=156/1.22) is the zone figure, but the preliminary plan caps Phase I at 65 (53 SFD + 12 SFA incl 9 MPDUs); against 65 the 62 approved is 4.6% below. Earlier manual note called the 65 only a transportation/APF condition; the site plan report does list a separate transportation condition (Phase I limited to 65 du) and LATR covers the first 65 permits, but preliminary plan condition 1 is a unit cap and the data table cites it as the permitted total. Caveat under the project rule (a cap equal to the applicant request is not a cap): the applicant applied for 184 lots and Phase I 65, but staff report documents lots removed in review for compatibility with Washington Grove. Plan level the preliminary report says the plan "does not take advantage of allowance. The plan is at a density of 3.10 dwelling units per gross acre; below the allowable density of 4.39" (12002022__item7a_121604_opt.txt p. 7). Site plan resolution 82006012C p. 1: approved 61, raised to 62 by amendment A.

doc_base: 75 = 6.27 ac x 12 du/ac (R-60/TDR-12 maximum with TDRs); zone base without TDRs is 31 (6.27 x 5)
comment: PDF p. 11 data table (confirmed on image): Maximum Density Allowed 75 (6.27 x 12 d.u./ac.) permitted vs 45 proposed; Base Density (6.27 ac. X 5 d.u./ac.) 31; Max. TDRs 44; TDRs provided (44 x 2/3) 29 = the minimum without waiver. Gross 6.27 ac used (0.13 ac floodplain not netted out). Master plan recommends R-60/TDR-12 "at a density of 12 dwelling units per acre" (p. 10), so no lower master-plan cap. 75 is reachable only by buying TDRs (every unit above 31), so being below 75 means buying fewer TDRs; the developer bought exactly the 2/3 minimum. Our base 75 matches the document maximum, but whether 75 or 31 is the right base before the MPDU bonus is a TDR judgment call (cf. the TDR flag in NOTES.md). The table arithmetic is odd (31 + 29 TDRs = 60, not 45; 6.27 x 10 is printed as 75). No reason stated for 45. Site has Gunners Branch stream valley buffer, floodplain and forest on its west edge; "Approximately 4.14 acres of the 6.27-acre site will be retained as open space" (p. 13) and 50% green area is required, but no passage links these to the unit count. Preliminary Plan 1-03067 approved the same 45.

doc_base: Plan level: 1,030,662 sf mapped residential density on the 16.64 ac tract (all phases); plan approved 625,594 sf for 279 du -> 459.6 du; Phase I (141 du, 325,924 sf) scaled = 232

reason_quote: The Sketch Plan Amendment will replace the previously approved mid-rise and high- rise residential at the eastern end of the site — which the Sector Plan envisioned as high density — with two-unit dwellings. The Applicant has justified the shift in unit type due to current market conditions.
comment: Sketch Plan amendment 32019007A data table (p. 6): residential mapped density 1,025,789 sf before, 1,030,662 sf (1.43 FAR) after, commercial dropped to 0; tract 16.64 ac (gross; site area after dedication 12.01 ac). Cap: Preliminary Plan 12020014A condition 1 (MCPB 25-144 p. 2) "limited to a maximum of 625,594 square feet of residential uses for a maximum of 279 dwelling units" = Phase I 107 TH + 34 two-over-two + Phase II 138 TH; this equals the applicant request, so not a cap under the NOTES rule. Sketch amendment p. 8: "The Sketch Plan Amendment density is still in conformance with the overall density limits in the Sector Plan." Phase I has no allocation of its own: Phase I resolution data table (p. 12) gives density per zone for the entire site, and the Phase I staff report (p. 13) says Phase I uses 325,924 sf "approximately 32%" of the 1,025,789 sf permitted for the entire Site. Phase I was the same in 2021, when the whole plan (745 du, Preliminary Plan 120200140) used the full mapped density; Phase I is below base only because Phase II was cut to townhouses in 2025, for the market reason quoted. Base 232 for Phase I is plan-level scaling (141 x 459.6/279), and it treats unbuilt Phase II as settled. The 15% MPDU share comes from the 2018 White Flint 2 Sector Plan.

doc_base: not stated (no density table in our three documents); our 60.1 = R-60 5.0 du/ac x 12.02 ac gross from the cover line
reason_quote: The selection of Corridor 1 necessitates substantial change to the proposed plan, including a reduction in residential units from 73 to 39.
comment: Another rule binds first: the Intercounty Connector (ICC) right-of-way reservation (SHA Corridor 1 and its US 29 interchange) took part of the site. Same page: "The applicant has filed the subject site plan amendment to accommodate the reduction in available land area." 2006 amendment B report (82005007__20061109_Fairland.txt p. 2): "the proposed ICC alignment and required berm resulted in the removal of all but 39 townhouses including five (5) MPDUs." The original site plan (82005007__item8_012705_opt.txt p. 3, condition 8c) was "Limit any future development on the site to 73 townhouse units". Base problems: (1) 12.02/12.08 ac is the gross site before the ICC took land; the remaining area is not given, so a base on usable land would be lower. (2) The original 73 TH on 12.08 ac is 6.04 du/ac, about the R-60 MPDU maximum (6.1 x 12.08 = 73.7), above the 5.0 standard (60.4), yet both reports say "the applicant is receiving no density bonus" (item5 p. 2, OCR "recerving"). Either that sentence is boilerplate or R-60 5.0 du/ac is not the base the Board used. The 73-unit report cover line reads "73 townhouses on 6.32 acres". 100% townhouses allowed under 59-C-1.621 for environmental/compatibility benefit (p. 7).

doc_base: CBD-3 optional method max 8.0 FAR on 108,557 sf gross tract = 868,456 sf; approved 5.29 FAR = 574,500 sf (515,000 sf residential + 59,500 sf retail) for 486 du -> 735 du (keeping retail share) or 763 du (8.0 FAR less the 59,500 sf retail)
doc_base_quote: the maximum density for optional method projects in the CBD-3 Zone is 8.0; the Project's density is 5.29 FAR.
comment: Data table (pp. 10-11): Gross Tract Area 108,557 sf, net tract 76,729 sf; FAR total 5.29, non-residential 0.55; residential GFA 515,000; 425 market + 61 MPDUs = 486. 5.29 = 574,500/108,557, so FAR is on gross tract. Only the resolution is in our files (no staff report, no Project Plan 920100020). Project Plan 920100020 approved 500 du and 200 ft; resolution p. 9: "The number of multi-family residential dwelling units has been reduced from the 500 to 486; and the building height has been reduced from 200 feet to 195 feet." The 500 looks like the applicant request, not a zoning cap. Whether the 8.0 FAR CBD-3 optional-method maximum already includes MPDU bonus density was not checked against the 2010 code. No reason stated. The 195-ft building is close to the 200-ft maximum (normally 143 ft, raised by the Board under 59-C-6.235(b)), so height may have bound, but the resolution does not say so.

doc_base: Development Plan G-801 (District Council, LMA rezoning to TS-M) caps residential by dwelling units, not FAR: 1,350 du (incl 169 MPDUs) for the whole 32.42-ac North Bethesda Center. Built/approved 1,312 (E 312, F 341, G 294, H 365). Plan-level base for Wentworth ~ 312 x 1,350/1,312 = 321. Parcel E share not found.
doc_base_quote: * Residential density in the Development Plan was limited only by dwelling units, not FAR
reason_quote: Together with previously approved and built residential buildings within the overall site, the total number of dwelling units will be 1,312, leaving a maximum of 38 dwelling units remaining under the G- 801 approval.
comment: Our 467.7 is the generic TS-M zone table: 3.0 FAR x 3.83 ac / an assumed 1,070 sf per unit, with no deduction for the 61,246 sf supermarket (deducting it gives ~410). But the site is under Development Plan G-801. Parcel F staff report (2008, same p. 14): "As part of the Development Plan, the District Council set limits for the residential and commercial development on the entire North Bethesda Center site, parsing the total amount of buildable area between the blocks"; the F/I/J table gives "Max. Density of Development (d.u.)* 500" permitted by the Development Plan. The Wentworth report (82005034__item6_072105_opt.txt p. 1, condition 1) requires compliance with "the certified Development Plan G-801" and says (p. 7) "The overall development for Bethesda Center North is approved for 1,350 residential dwelling units"; Preliminary Plan 120040490 condition 1 (82008011__North-Bethesda-Preliminary-Plan-No-120040490.txt p. 7) limits the site to 1,350 units. The 2005 Wentworth staff report PDF we have is 8 pages with no data table, so Parcel E own allocation under G-801 is not in our files. Plan level the four residential parcels reach 1,312 of 1,350 (2.8% below the cap), so Wentworth is very likely at or near its Development Plan allocation, not 33% below base. Fix: treat as phase of a capped plan, base ~321 (or the Parcel E allocation if the Development Plan is found).

doc_base: 1,017 du "Maximum Units (w/ MPDU's)" = 32.6952 ac gross x 43,560 / 1,400 sf (RH, whole Woodlake site plan 8-71011); 593 = 534 existing 1971 apartments + 59 new townhouses. For the 59 TH: leftover base ~300 (1,017/1.22 = 834, less 534 existing) or ~101 on the 3.95 ac net townhouse area; our scaled 83 = 834 x 59/593.
reason_quote: The proposal today is for the “infill” development of approximately 5.32 acres of the 32.69 acre Woodlake site
comment: Data table read from PDF p. 3 (printed p. 12; OCR scrambles the columns): Allowed/Required 1,017 units; Proposed 534 Existing Units, 59 Townhouses, 593 Total Units; MPDU 12.5% x 59 = 7.37 -> 8. p. 4: combined with Ventura (49.35 ac) 1,535 allowed vs 796. So approved_units 593 is the whole Woodlake site, not the project. Right numbers for the report project: approved 59 TH incl 8 MPDUs on 5.32 ac (net 3.95 ac per p. 4 table). Base for the 59: our 83 scales the site base by 59/593 as if the 534 old apartments were part of the project. Better: the base left for new units, 834 - 534 = 300 (or 483 if 1,017 is taken as the pre-bonus figure). Staff also required the infill to meet density on its own net area (item2 p. 5: "The application does meet current standards for MPDUs, density and green space within the-net and gross parcels"): 3.95 ac x 43,560/1,400 = 123 with MPDUs = 101 before bonus (5.32 ac gives 136). All are above 59, so it is below base under any reading; ratio is 1.4 to 5. The 1.22 division assumes "w/ MPDU's" means the bonus is inside 1,017; RH zone text not checked. Transportation condition (item2 p. 2) "Limit future additional development on the site (on Parcel J) to 59 townhouse condominium units" equals the request, not a zoning cap. No reason stated for 59. The quoted passage says the townhouses fill the former open space (tennis court, wooded/grassy area) of an existing apartment complex; master plan context favors ownership units (item2b p. 8: "Providing home ownership opportunities in Woodlake, a garden apartment community, even if the new units were not detached, would be consistent with the goals of the master plan.").
